patient.title: Gemcitabine and cisplatin · lung cancer
patient.purpose: These two chemotherapy medicines aim to slow or shrink advanced non-small-cell lung cancer and help control symptoms. Benefit is not guaranteed. Your team explains the aim for your own situation.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, unusual bleeding, breathlessness, rash, swelling or reduced urine promptly.
risks: Rare serious lung or kidney injury

agents.name: Cisplatin
agents.explanation: Cisplatin forms links in DNA that interfere with copying and repair. This helps stop cancer cells dividing, but healthy tissues may also be affected. Kidney protection with fluids and monitoring is central to cisplatin treatment.
agents.watch: Report ringing in the ears, hearing changes, numbness or loss of function. Tell the team if you cannot drink, are passing less urine or become swollen or breathless during fluids.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Hearing changes or tinnitus, which can persist
Numbness or tingling, which can persist
Electrolyte changes and need for hydration

phases.label: Chemotherapy course
phases.detail: A cycle lasts 21 days (3 weeks). Day 1: gemcitabine and cisplatin. Day 8: gemcitabine alone after separate blood tests and review. Days 9–21: no scheduled chemotherapy. The usual planned course is 4–6 cycles, with earlier changes for progression or unacceptable effects.

phases.label: Response and next-plan review
phases.detail: Your team weighs scan results, symptoms and side effects before deciding to continue, stop or change treatment. No automatic immunotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery phase is included.

timeline.label: Time at home
timeline.text: Effects vary; report concerns without waiting for the next cycle.

day_groups.title: Day 1 treatment
day_groups.body: Gemcitabine and cisplatin after blood tests and review.
day_groups.action: Confirm symptoms, blood results and support plan.

day_groups.title: Day 8 treatment
day_groups.body: Gemcitabine alone if blood tests and review allow.
day_groups.action: Do not assume Day 1 clearance covers Day 8.

day_groups.title: Recovery and review
day_groups.body: Effects vary; no guaranteed recovery day.

support.title: Prevent and treat sickness
support.text: Follow one written anti-sickness prescription, including any tablets for home and rescue treatment. Day 8 gemcitabine has a separate lower-risk anti-sickness plan. Cisplatin needs prescribed IV hydration, electrolyte replacement and kidney, hearing and nerve checks. Follow your own fluid advice; tell the team if you have heart failure or a fluid restriction.

support.title: Check before each dose
support.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before treatment and on Day 1; blood count and creatinine again before Day 8. Symptoms are reviewed before each dose. Hearing tests are arranged when needed. Scans follow your consultant’s individual plan, not a fixed universal interval.

support.title: Keep your SACT card with you
support.text: Show your treatment card to any healthcare professional. Keep daytime and out-of-hours oncology numbers accessible.

questions.a: Usually Day 1 for both medicines and Day 8 for gemcitabine in each 21-day cycle. Your unit confirms actual appointments and blood tests.

questions.q: Does a delayed dose mean treatment failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, kidney results or symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Will I also receive immunotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery?
questions.a: This guide covers standalone chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC. If nivolumab is part of your treatment before surgery, use the separate 00849 guide for gemcitabine/cisplatin; that is a different three-cycle plan.

questions.q: Who do I call if I feel unwell?
questions.a: Use the oncology number on your treatment summary or SACT card. Ask for a daytime and out-of-hours number before leaving. Do not use the QR website as an emergency contact service.

items.title: Which plan is this?
items.text: This guide covers standalone chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC. If nivolumab is part of your treatment before surgery, use the separate 00849 guide for gemcitabine/cisplatin; that is a different three-cycle plan.

items.title: How the medicines work
items.text: Gemcitabine interferes with the DNA building blocks a dividing cell needs. Platinum makes links within DNA that disrupt copying and repair. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.

items.title: Benefits and alternatives
items.text: A randomized study in previously untreated advanced lung cancer compared gemcitabine with cisplatin against gemcitabine with carboplatin. Both approaches showed anticancer activity. Treatment choice also depends on kidney function, hearing, nerves, blood counts and your preferences. Ask about alternative systemic treatments, clinical trials, symptom-focused care and the choice not to proceed.

items.title: Time in the unit
items.text: Gemcitabine runs through a drip over 30 minutes on Days 1 and 8. Cisplatin runs over 60 minutes on Day 1, with fluids and electrolytes before and afterwards according to your prescribed plan. Blood tests, pharmacy preparation, support medicines and review add to the visit time.

items.title: Day 8 is a separate decision
items.text: Blood count, kidney and liver tests before treatment and on Day 1; blood count and creatinine again before Day 8. Symptoms are reviewed before each dose. Hearing tests are arranged when needed. Scans follow your consultant’s individual plan, not a fixed universal interval.

chapters.title: Side effects and action
chapters.intro: Effects differ between people; report new symptoms early.

items.title: When to call now
items.text: Call your oncology team immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, shaking chills, new breathlessness, chest pain, unusual bleeding, very little urine, severe rash or blistering, or vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down. Use your unit’s temperature threshold and emergency instructions. Do not wait until the next visit.

items.title: During a drip
items.text: Tell the nurse immediately about rash, flushing, chills, breathlessness, chest discomfort, faintness or pain/swelling around the cannula.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Tests can detect changes before you notice symptoms. Normal results at the last visit do not rule out a problem now.

chapters.title: Everyday life
chapters.intro: Plan support around how you feel.

items.title: Eating and drinking
items.text: Ask for help with nausea, appetite and mouth soreness. Follow your own fluid plan and tell the team if you cannot drink.

items.title: Medicines and fertility
items.text: Bring a full list of medicines and supplements. Discuss pregnancy prevention, breastfeeding and fertility before treatment.

items.title: Activity and help
items.text: Balance gentle activity with rest. Ask your team for help with symptoms, transport, work and caring responsibilities.

chapters.title: Checking progress
chapters.intro: The treatment plan is reviewed throughout the course.

items.title: Scans and symptoms
items.text: Your consultant chooses scan timing according to the cancer and treatment plan. Blood tests primarily check safety and do not by themselves show whether treatment is working.

items.title: After chemotherapy
items.text: Agree the next treatment or follow-up plan, ongoing symptom support and whom to contact. Some nerve or hearing effects can persist.

items.title: Keep your SACT card with you
items.text: Show your treatment card to any healthcare professional. Keep daytime and out-of-hours oncology numbers accessible.

chapters.title: Side effects and action
chapters.intro: Effects differ between people; report new symptoms early.

items.title: When to call now
items.text: Call your oncology team immediately for fever or suddenly feeling unwell, shaking chills, new breathlessness, chest pain, unusual bleeding, very little urine, severe rash or blistering, or vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down. Use your unit’s temperature threshold and emergency instructions. Do not wait until the next visit.

items.title: During a drip
items.text: Tell the nurse immediately about rash, flushing, chills, breathlessness, chest discomfort, faintness or pain/swelling around the cannula.

items.title: Blood and organ checks
items.text: Tests can detect changes before you notice symptoms. Normal results at the last visit do not rule out a problem now.

chapters.title: Everyday life
chapters.intro: Plan support around how you feel.

items.title: Eating and drinking
items.text: Ask for help with nausea, appetite and mouth soreness. Follow your own fluid plan and tell the team if you cannot drink.

items.title: Medicines and fertility
items.text: Bring a full list of medicines and supplements. Discuss pregnancy prevention, breastfeeding and fertility before treatment.

items.title: Activity and help
items.text: Balance gentle activity with rest. Ask your team for help with symptoms, transport, work and caring responsibilities.

chapters.title: Checking progress
chapters.intro: The treatment plan is reviewed throughout the course.

items.title: Scans and symptoms
items.text: Your consultant chooses scan timing according to the cancer and treatment plan. Blood tests primarily check safety and do not by themselves show whether treatment is working.

items.title: After chemotherapy
items.text: Agree the next treatment or follow-up plan, ongoing symptom support and whom to contact. Some nerve or hearing effects can persist.

items.title: Before leaving the clinic
items.text: Ask the team to complete your treatment aim, planned cycles, contact numbers and next appointment. Keep this summary with your SACT card.

items.title: Check your understanding
items.text: In your own words: which medicines are given on Day 1 and Day 8, which symptoms need a call today, and which number will you use out of hours?

evidence.title: Why this combination may be offered
evidence.summary: A randomized study in previously untreated advanced lung cancer compared gemcitabine with cisplatin against gemcitabine with carboplatin. Both approaches showed anticancer activity. Treatment choice also depends on kidney function, hearing, nerves, blood counts and your preferences.
